Yet the challenges and struggles that come with war come to the individual. Can a righteous, peaceful individual maintain those qualities in an atmosphere of hatred, along with an environment where life is not respected nor God revered? The answer to this question is also found in this section of the Book of Mormon. We are given the example of Captain Moroni. He did not want to shed blood, but he loved peace and desired to keep the commandments. Yet he spent most of his adult life in war. His profession appeared to be that of a military leader. He took good men into battle, and he had to watch many of them suffer and die.

quotes.text: Part of the reason we may not have sufficient priesthood bearers to save the Constitution, let alone to shake the powers of hell, is because unlike Moroni, I fear, our souls do not joy in keeping our country free, and we are not firm in the faith of Christ, nor have we sworn with an oath to defend our rights and the liberty of our country.
